pull.title: MINOR: Track share fetch offset metadata per DelayedShareFetch instead of SharePartition
pull.body:
DelayedShareFetch estimates the available bytes for minBytes by
comparing the end offset with the cached LogOffsetMetadata of the fetch
offset. The cache was kept on SharePartition, so it outlived the request
which populated it. A partition that is read but trimmed from the
response, or whose request fails, kept a valid cache entry although its
fetch offset did not advance, which requires resets and made the read
path depend on state left behind by earlier requests.

Keep the metadata inside DelayedShareFetch for the lifetime of the
request, as DelayedFetch does with FetchPartitionStatus. The retries of
tryComplete in purgatory still avoid reading from the log, and the cache
can no longer go stale across requests, so the remote fetch reset is not
needed.

Add ShareConsumerFairnessTest to verify that two partitions with a deep
backlog are both served under record_limit acquire mode.

There are also cases where if a record is released where it was earlier
fetch then request has to go through timeout to fetch data. Those
scenarios are also handled by this fix.

Reviewers: Andrew Schofield <aschofield@confluent.io>, Abhinav Dixit
 <adixit@confluent.io>

This seems to be a problem. The PR quietly stopped testing the branch of `isMinBytesSatisfied` that actually counts bytes against fetch.min.bytes.

The three branches ->

For each partition, [isMinBytesSatisfied](https://github.com/apache/kafka/blob/ae962680085cd125f52ef7b0d466b176c4048a0a/core/src/main/java/kafka/server/share/DelayedShareFetch.java#L594-L638) compares the cached fetch-offset metadata F with the end-offset (HWM) metadata E:

1. F is past E: complete immediately.
2. F is on an older segment than E: complete immediately, without counting bytes. This is the “older-segment shortcut”.
3. F and E on the same segment: add min(E.position − F.position, partitionMaxBytes) to a running total. At the end, complete only if total >= minBytes.
Branch 3 is what implements fetch.min.bytes. 

The PR changed where F comes from:

trunk: F came from a mocked `sp.fetchOffsetMetadata(...)`, returning (offset 0, segment 1, position 0). The helper mockTopicIdPartitionToReturnDataEqualToMinBytes put E at (offset 1, segment 1, position minBytes). Same segment, so the tests counted exactly minBytes bytes and completed right at the threshold, which is what the helper is named for.
PR: that mock is gone, and F now comes from the log read result. buildLogReadResult’s default is [(0, segment 0, 0)](https://github.com/apache/kafka/blob/ae962680085cd125f52ef7b0d466b176c4048a0a/core/src/test/java/kafka/server/share/SharePartitionManagerTest.java#L3291). Segment 0 is older than segment 1, so isMinBytesSatisfied returns true through branch 2 before it counts anything.

Seven tests changed path this way. None is named for minBytes, which is how the loss went unnoticed:

DelayedShareFetchTest:
testDelayedShareFetchTryCompleteReturnsTrue
both testPartitionMaxBytesFromUniformStrategy
testTryCompleteAsyncCompletion

SharePartitionManagerTest:
testAcknowledgeCompletesDelayedShareFetchRequest
testReleaseSessionCompletesDelayedShareFetchRequest
testSharePartitionPartialInitializationFailure

On trunk they were the suite’s only positive tests of branch 3. They still pass on the PR, just through branch 2.

issue_comments.body:
Ran some performance tests through claude to find if it doesn't cause any regression. Results:

| Scenario | Metric | Trunk | This change |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Throughput** (3M records preloaded, consumed at full speed) | records/s | 249,667 / 266,785 | 268,192 / 255,450 |
| | MB/s | 47.6 / 50.9 | 51.2 / 48.7 |
| | broker CPU, consume phase (s) | 14.8 / 14.3 | 14.0 / 14.4 |
| **minBytes** (producer capped at 5,000 rec/s, `fetch.min.bytes=1MB`, `fetch.max.wait.ms=500`, 300k records) | records/s | 4,973 / 4,996 | 4,980 / 5,017 |
| | broker CPU, total (s) | 28.4 / 25.7 | 28.3 / 22.6 |
| **Segment roll** (`segment.bytes=1MB`, ~50 segments per partition, 1.5M records produced and consumed concurrently) | records/s | 128,733 / 126,657 | 126,957 / 137,665 |
| | MB/s | 24.6 / 24.2 | 24.2 / 26.3 |
| | broker CPU, total (s) | 15.6 / 16.2 | 15.9 / 15.1 |

| | Throughput | minBytes | Segment roll |
|---|---|---|---|
| Partitions | 6 | 6 | 6 |
| Consumers | 8 | 8 | 8 |
| Records | 3,000,000 | 300,000 | 1,500,000 |
| Data | 572 MB | 57 MB | 286 MB |
| Producer | Preloaded first at full speed, consumer started afterwards | Capped at 5,000 records/s total, running concurrently with the consumers | Full speed, running concurrently with the consumers |
| Consumer overrides | none | `fetch.min.bytes=1048576`, `fetch.max.wait.ms=500` | none |
| Topic config | defaults (1 GB segments) | defaults | `segment.bytes=1048576` (~50 segments per partition) |
| Run length | ~11–12 s consuming | ~60 s | ~11–12 s |

> Thanks for the PR. A few comments. Also I think it will be good to add a unit test where a retry in `tryComplete` at the same offset doesn’t re-read, and a new request does.

Added test.

MINOR: Track share fetch offset metadata per DelayedShareFetch instead of SharePartition

DelayedShareFetch estimates the available bytes for minBytes by comparing the
end offset with the cached LogOffsetMetadata of the fetch offset. The cache was
kept on SharePartition, so it outlived the request which populated it. A
partition that is read but trimmed from the response, or whose request fails,
kept a valid cache entry although its fetch offset did not advance, which
required resets for remote fetch and made the read path depend on state left
behind by earlier requests.

Keep the metadata inside DelayedShareFetch for the lifetime of the request, as
DelayedFetch does with FetchPartitionStatus. The retries of tryComplete in
purgatory still avoid reading from the log, and the cache can no longer go
stale across requests, so the remote fetch reset is not needed.

Add ShareConsumerFairnessTest to verify that two partitions with a deep backlog
are both served under record_limit acquire mode.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

MINOR: Addressing review comments

Consume all the records in ShareConsumerFairnessTest instead of limiting the
number of polls and verify the progress of the other partition when the first
partition completes, move the class javadoc before the annotations, fix the
javadoc indentation of the fetch offset metadata cache, remove the unreachable
null check on the cached offset metadata and the test comments which referred
to the removed SharePartition cache stubs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
